items.title: [kiwitcms] Kiwi TCMS account confirmation open redirect through protocol-relative URLs
items.summary: SummaryIn Kiwi TCMS version 16.1, the fix for CVE-2026-54724 (open redirect via unvalidated next parameter) in the account confirmation endpoint is incomplete. The validation uses startswith("/") to check if the redirect URL is local, but this is bypassed by protocol-relative URLs like //evil.com which start with / but redirect the browser to an external attacker-controlled domain. 16.1’s incomplete mitigation still allows protocol-relative destinations and earlier releases lack the mitigation.Vulnerable CodeIn tcms/kiwi_auth/views.py, the Confirm view (line ~113):def get_redirect_url(self, *args, **kwargs):    self.url = self.request.GET.get("next", reverse("core-views-index"))    if not self.url.startswith("/"):        self.url = reverse("core-views-index")The check startswith("/") passes for //evil.com because it begins with /, but browsers interpret //evil.com as a protocol-relative URL that redirects to https://evil.com (or http://evil.com depending on the current page's protocol).Proof of ConceptGET /confirm/<activation_key>/?next=//evil.com/phishing HTTP/1.1Host: kiwi.example.comResponse:HTTP/1.1 302 FoundLocation: //evil.com/phishingThe browser follows the redirect to https://evil.com/phishing.Verification:>>> url = "//evil.com/phishing">>> url.startswith("/")True  # passes the check!ImpactAn attacker can craft a confirmation link that, after the user confirms their account, redirects them to a phishing page. This is useful for:Credential phishing (fake login page on attacker domain)Malware delivery after trusted actionSocial engineering (user trusts the link because it's from the legitimate Kiwi TCMS instance)The attack requires sending a crafted activation link to a user who is registering, or intercepting/predicting the activation key.Suggested FixUse Django's url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme() utility instead of a simple startswith check:from django.utils.http import url_has_allowed_host_and_schemedef get_redirect_url(self, *args, **kwargs):    self.url = self.request.GET.get("next", reverse("core-views-index"))    if not url_has_allowed_host_and_scheme(        self.url,        allowed_hosts={self.request.get_host()},        require_https=self.request.is_secure(),    ):        self.url = reverse("core-views-index")This properly rejects protocol-relative URLs, absolute URLs to other hosts, and other bypass patterns.Fixed in Version 16.2Referenceshttps://github.com/kiwitcms/Kiwi/security/advisories/GHSA-gcwf-c25f-p9rvhttps://github.com/kiwitcms/Kiwi/security/advisories/GHSA-hmj5-jm8h-h9fhhttps://github.com/kiwitcms/Kiwi/pull/4458https://github.com/kiwitcms/Kiwi/commit/65d8f7c2743d7f06a4fca77c060b9d561f02f948https://github.com/kiwitcms/Kiwi/releases/tag/v16.2https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gcwf-c25f-p9rv

items.title: [code-graph-rag] Code Graph RAG structural tools follow out-of-root symlinks
items.summary: A remote/local attacker who can get a symbolic link included in a source-code repository that code-graph-rag analyzes can cause the structural_search and structural_replace tools (backed by AstGrepService, exposed both as MCP tools and as agentic AI tools) to read and -- via structural_replace with dry_run=False -- overwrite arbitrary files outside the configured project root, because the tool's path-containment check (should_skip_path/_classify_file) is performed lexically on the unresolved path and never checks Path.is_symlink() or calls .resolve(), unlike the project's own (correct) validate_project_path decorator used elsewhere.Tested at commit 90a3ed3cbdc7d3bb8036985b851cc7c9a3ba9c57 (pyproject version 0.0.550), current main at test time. Confirmed this commit already contains the fix for the prior advisory (GHSA-vvr2-h2jp-838m: paginated read_file path traversal) and the newer HTTP-MCP bearer-auth gate (_validate_http_exposure in codebase_rag/mcp/server.py) -- this is a distinct, still-open issue on top of those fixes, in a different component with a different root cause and a strictly worse impact (write, not just read).DetailsAstGrepService (codebase_rag/tools/ast_grep_service.py) backs both the structural_search and structural_replace MCP/agentic tools. It enumerates candidate files with os.walk() and gates each path only through should_skip_path():codebase_rag/tools/ast_grep_service.py:84-109 (_iter_source_files) -- walks self.project_root with os.walk(); every non-directory dirent returned (including a symlink pointing anywhere on disk) is treated as an in-scope file.codebase_rag/tools/ast_grep_service.py:61-82 (_classify_file) -- the only containment check is should_skip_path(...) followed by abs_path.relative_to(self.project_root) (line 82); abs_path is never resolved, so this check is purely lexical/string-based.codebase_rag/utils/path_utils.py:80-109 (should_skip_path) and codebase_rag/utils/path_utils.py:35-37 (cached_relative_path) -- computes rel_path = file_path.relative_to(repo_path) without ever calling .resolve() or Path.is_symlink().Read sink: codebase_rag/tools/ast_grep_service.py:143-144 (search) -- source = self._read(abs_path) calls path.read_text(), which Python follows through the symlink to its real target.Write sink: codebase_rag/tools/ast_grep_service.py:187-208 (replace), line 208 -- abs_path.write_text(new_source, ...) when dry_run=False, again following the symlink and overwriting the real target file's content.This is inconsistent with how the rest of the codebase handles the exact same class of risk. The file read/write/edit tools (file_reader.py, file_writer.py, file_editor.py) are all protected by validate_project_path (codebase_rag/decorators.py:73-75):full_path = (self.project_root / file_path_str).resolve()project_root = self.project_root.resolve()full_path.relative_to(project_root).resolve() follows symlinks before the containment check runs, so those tools correctly reject an out-of-root target. path_utils.py's own absolute_path_within_project_root() (codebase_rag/utils/path_utils.py:156-176) documents the same principle explicitly in its docstring: "The resolve() calls are load-bearing: containment is checked lexically, so an unresolved .. segment or symlink would escape the root." -- but should_skip_path()/AstGrepService never applies that pattern.Reachability: structural_search (codebase_rag/tools/structural_search.py:24-46) carries no requires_approval flag at all -- in AI-orchestrator mode the model can call it autonomously with no human confirmation. structural_replace (codebase_rag/tools/structural_editor.py:52-57) is marked requires_approval=True, but that flag is only enforced by pydantic-ai's own agent loop -- the MCP server path bypasses it entirely: MCPToolsRegistry.structural_replace (codebase_rag/mcp/tools.py:586-596) calls self._structural_editor_tool.function(...) directly, registered with no approval concept at codebase_rag/mcp/tools.py:369-388. Any MCP client that can call tools can invoke structural_replace with dry_run=False in one shot.Proof of ConceptDynamically confirmed against the installed package (mgclient/pymgclient mocked, as in the prior advisory's own PoC, since the Memgraph native client isn't needed for this code path).mkdir -p /tmp/poc_symlink/safe-project-rootcat > /tmp/poc_symlink/outside-secret.py << 'EOF'API_TOKEN = "sk-live-EXAMPLE-NOT-A-REAL-SECRET-1234567890"def get_token():    return API_TOKENEOFln -s /tmp/poc_symlink/outside-secret.py /tmp/poc_symlink/safe-project-root/linked_module.pyimport sysfrom pathlib import Pathfrom unittest.mock import MagicMocksys.modules["mgclient"] = MagicMock()sys.modules["pymgclient"] = MagicMock()from codebase_rag.tools.ast_grep_service import AstGrepServiceSAFE_ROOT = "/tmp/poc_symlink/safe-project-root"svc = AstGrepService(project_root=SAFE_ROOT)matches = svc.search(pattern="API_TOKEN", language="python")# -> match in reported file='linked_module.py' text='API_TOKEN'  (read escape)changes

items.title: [gpustack] GPUStack: Authentication bypass via trusted loopback source (reverse-proxy TCP peer or X-GPUStack-Real-IP header) grants unauthenticated admin
items.summary: ImpactIn GPUStack before v2.2.0, get_current_user (in gpustack/api/auth.py) promotes any request whose source is considered loopback to the built-in administrator account when force_auth_localhost is False (the default). The "source" is derived by client_ip_getter, which can be made to report 127.0.0.1 without any credentials in two ways:Same-host reverse proxy (TCP peer). In the canonical self-hosted shape —GPUStack behind a same-host reverse proxy with proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:<port> — every remote request arrives at GPUStack with TCPpeer 127.0.0.1, so the loopback auto-admin branch fires. No header orcredential is required. Verified end-to-end against HEAD 6bee5883.X-GPUStack-Real-IP header. A forged X-GPUStack-Real-IP: 127.0.0.1header can cause the request source to be treated as loopback.Either path yields full, unauthenticated administrative access over the network: enumerate and modify users, models, workers, and configuration; mint persistent admin API keys (scope ["*"], valid from any source IP thereafter); read worker credentials and cloud/provider secrets. Combined with admin-only functionality such as POST /v2/inference-backends/from yaml, this leads to code execution on worker hosts.This vulnerability has been observed exploited in the wild against a v2.1.1 deployment (attacker-created custom backends running reverse shells).Root causeTrusting the network source of a request (socket peer, or a client-controllable header) as an authentication signal. When GPUStack is fronted by a same-host reverse proxy, the socket peer is always loopback, so the "localhost is trusted" assumption no longer holds.PatchesFixed in gpustack 2.2.0: the loopback auto-admin path was removed and client-IP / forwarding-header handling was hardened. Upgrade to 2.2.0 or later.WorkaroundsSet force_auth_localhost=true to require authentication even for loopbackrequests.Ensure the reverse proxy / gateway cannot cause GPUStack to treat externaltraffic as loopback, and strip any client-supplied X-GPUStack-Real-IPheader at the edge.Keep the API off untrusted networks (VPN / edge authentication).Remediation (in the fix)Do not derive authentication from the request's network source. Remove implicit loopback-based admin, and only accept a real client-IP header from an authenticated/trusted gateway (never from arbitrary clients).CreditIndependently reported by Nikko Enggaliano; Wei Yunzhou; and Rui Yang & Haoyu Wang (Johns Hopkins University). Active in the-wild exploitation was reported by Javier Sixto (ulex.fr).Referenceshttps://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/security/advisories/GHSA-gj9m-f8ph-pmhrhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-102895https://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/pull/5346https://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/commit/53f42a6a553542974396d16a4ff6b12bcbedb48dhttps://github.com/gpustack/gpustack/releases/tag/v2.2.0https://www.cisa.gov/known-exploited-vulnerabilities-catalog?field_cve=CVE-2026-102895https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-gj9m-f8ph-pmhr

items.title: [urwid] Urwid: handle_short_request() crashes on non-ASCII POST body (UnicodeEncodeError DoS)
items.summary: SummaryThe handle_short_request() function in urwid/display/web.py raises an unhandled UnicodeEncodeError when processing a POST request body containing non-ASCII bytes. The function reads POST input and encodes it to ASCII before writing to a named pipe. Any byte value above 0x7F causes the CGI process to exit with an unhandled exception, returning an HTTP 500 error to the client. Additionally, a file descriptor opened earlier in the same function is not closed before the exception propagates, causing a file descriptor leak for the lifetime of the CGI process.A second instance of missing exception handling exists in the polling update path, where non-UTF-8 socket output causes an unhandled UnicodeDecodeError.ImpactAn attacker who observes a valid X-Urwid-ID session token (transmitted in plaintext HTTP response headers) can send repeated POST requests containing non-ASCII bytes to the urwid CGI endpoint. Each malformed request causes the CGI handler to crash with HTTP 500. This results in a Denial of Service (DoS) for legitimate users using the urwid web interface.Affected Versionsurwid <= 4.0.6PatchesFixed in urwid 4.0.7. Users should upgrade to version 4.0.7 or later.WorkaroundsNo direct workaround exists short of disabling the urwid web display interface.Referenceshttps://github.com/urwid/urwid/security/advisories/GHSA-cp25-j9x5-p5xmhttps://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-103022https://github.com/urwid/urwid/pull/1201https://github.com/urwid/urwid/commit/b79d9a96843a6f5950bb2bfab5d059bdc61c538bhttps://github.com/urwid/urwid/releases/tag/4.0.7https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-cp25-j9x5-p5xm

items.title: [fast-agent-mcp] fast-agent: `fast-agent serve` binds HTTP to 0.0.0.0 with no authentication by default; with --shell this is unauthenticated remote command execution
items.summary: Summaryfast-agent serve exposes the agent over MCP. By default it uses HTTP transport bound to 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces) on port 8000 with no authentication (auth=None) and prints no warning. Any host that can reach the port can call the exposed agent tool. When the server is started with --shell (which is -x, the flag used in the README quickstart uvx fast-agent mcp@latest -x), the agent has a local execute shell tool, so an unauthenticated remote client can drive the agent into running arbitrary OS commands — unauthenticated RCE.Affected codecli/commands/serve.py — transport defaults to HTTP; --host defaults to 0.0.0.0; port 8000.mcp/server/agent_server.py — auth_provider = None unless FAST_AGENT_SERVE_OAUTH=huggingface;run_async(transport="http", host=host, ...) with host defaulting to 0.0.0.0.tools/local_shell_executor.py — the shell tool runs commands via create_subprocess_shell.Verified (live, faithful — published 0.7.20 in Docker python:3.13-slim, stock unauthenticated client)Unauthenticated exposure (core defect): a client with no Authorization header completedinitialize and tools/list (-> ['agent']) against http://HOST:8000/mcp. Model-independent.Unauthenticated RCE with --shell, demonstrated two ways:Real production model (gpt-4o-mini): a single plain-language message asking the agent to runa command via its shell tool -> the model autonomously called execute and the command output(process identity showing it ran as root, the hostname, and the first lines of a sensitivesystem file) was returned to the unauthenticated caller.Key-free deterministic (passthrough model): the tool-call directive invoked the shell tooldirectly, same result.The server-side permission prompt did not block this in non-interactive serve mode.Proof of conceptEnvironment: Docker python:3.13-slim, pip install fast-agent-mcp -> 0.7.20.# server (real model + the documented shell flag; 0.0.0.0 is also the built-in default)OPENAI_API_KEY=*** fast-agent serve --model gpt-4o-mini --shell --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000#  -> "Uvicorn running on http://0.0.0.0:8000"   (no auth, no warning)# attacker: unauthenticated MCP HTTP client (NO Authorization header) to http://HOST:8000/mcp#   initialize()                       -> 200 OK (server fast-agent-MCP-Server 0.7.20)#   tools/list                         -> ['agent']#   tools/call name="agent" arguments={"message":#       "Using your execute/shell tool, run exactly this command and return its raw stdout: "#       "id; echo PWNED=$(hostname); cat /etc/passwd | head -2"}## response returned to the UNAUTHENTICATED caller:#   uid=0(root) gid=0(root) groups=0(root)#   PWNED=<host>#   <first lines of /etc/passwd>Also reproduced key-free with --model passthrough and the message ***CALL_TOOL execute {"command":"id"} (passthrough invokes the tool deterministically). Full transcript + client scripts were sent by email.ImpactAn unauthenticated client that can reach the serve port controls the agent: with --shell this is remote command execution as the server user; without --shell it is unauthenticated use of the operator's LLM and any configured MCP servers' tools. The 0.0.0.0 default makes the server reachable beyond localhost as soon as it runs on a non-isolated host. Preconditions (serve + shell) are noted above and are why I defer the exact rating to you.RemediationDefault the bind host to 127.0.0.1; require an explicit --host 0.0.0.0 opt-in for non-loopback.Print a loud warning when binding a non-loopback interface without authentication.Referenceshttps://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/security/advisories/GHSA-9vhv-g5hf-m7m7https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-102610https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/pull/828https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/commit/ba99f89c3ec7f1ef1c8b1ebce381c12b60dfea29https://github.com/evalstate/fast-agent/releases/tag/v0.7.21https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-9vhv-g5hf-m7m7

items.title: [zizmor] zizmor: Debug logging prints available GitHub credentials in cleartext
items.summary: Summaryzizmor 1.27.0 exposes GitHub access tokens in cleartext when debug-level logging is enabled. Tokens supplied via environment variables (GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, ZIZMOR_GITHUB_TOKEN), or the corresponding command-line options (--gh-token, --github-token, --zizmor-github-token) are included in the debug representation of the parsed application configuration and written to stderr.The affected logging is enabled by a single -v/--verbose or an applicable RUST_LOG directive. DetailsThe issue was introduced in commit 919bea46, merged through PR #2180. Version 1.26.1 and earlier are unaffected. Version 1.27.0 is the first and only affected release.zizmor accepts GitHub credentials to perform authenticated GitHub API requests for the purposes of retrieving remote GitHub repositories and performing online audits that may require resolving information such as action references, commits, or repository metadata. A GitHub credential is used to avoid unauthenticated API limits and, when applicable, provide access to private repositories.PR #2180 was intended to improve the experience around zizmor’s implicit offline mode. It also moved the CLI types into a dedicated module and added a debug log of the fully parsed App value:tracing::debug!("app: {app:?}"); This diagnostic is useful for understanding the effective CLI state, including whether offline operation was explicit or inferred. However, the same commit added derived Debug implementations to App, NetworkArgs, and GitHubToken(String).Before the debug event is emitted, the compatibility token aliases are merged into app.network.gh_token.The resulting stderr contains the token verbatim. Explicit --offline clears the token before the debug event, but normal online operation and --no-online-audits retain it.PoCUsing zizmor at v1.27.0:GH_TOKEN=gho_ZIZMOR_MRE zizmor --verbose example.ymlwill emitDEBUG zizmor: app: App { input: InputArgs { inputs: ["example.yml"], collect: [Default], strict_collection: false }, audit: AuditArgs { fix: None, pedantic: false, persona: Regular, min_severity: None, min_confidence: None, no_ignores: false }, output: OutputArgs { verbose: Verbosity { verbose: 1, quiet: 0, phantom: PhantomData<clap_verbosity_flag::InfoLevel> }, format: Plain, no_progress: false, color: None, render_links: Auto, show_audit_urls: Auto, no_exit_codes: false, naches: false }, network: NetworkArgs { offline: false, gh_token: Some(GitHubToken("gho_ZIZMOR_MRE")), github_token: None, zizmor_github_token: None, gh_hostname: Standard("github.com"), no_online_audits: false, cache_dir: "/Users/shaan/.cache/zizmor" }, args: GlobalArgs { lsp: LspArgs { lsp: false, stdio: false }, config: None, no_config: false, completions: None, thanks: false, help: (), version: () } }ImpactIn practice, the impact of this vulnerability should be mediated by GitHub's own layered defenses, including secret redaction in Actions logs and automatic credential revocation in issue/PR/etc. comments. However, zizmor itself should never log sensitive materials, and so the behavior is still considered vulnerable even if compensating controls exist in downstream systems.An affected user must enable debug logging while supplying a GitHub credential, and the resulting stderr must be available to another party. Plausible disclosure channels include a public bug report, CI log or artifact, or terminal capture. A potential attacker only needs permission to read the disclosed logs.The resulting impact depends on the token's scopes, repository access, and lifetime. A minimally scoped token may only expose public read-only data, while a broader OAuth token or personal access token may permit private-repository or modification of repositories, packages, workflows, or organization resources. The default informational logging level is unaffected. Exploitation requires debug logging and subsequent log exposure, which limits likelihood.Notably, because zizmor’s bug-report template asks users to rerun commands with --verbose and paste the complete logs, this can result in credentials being copied into public issues or other support channels.Referenceshttps://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/security/advisories/GHSA-f42p-wjw5-97qhhttps://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/pull/2213https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/pull/2215https://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/commit/0731e01706af273be860d3d221e4d122e6741b6fhttps://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/commit/724d0e86f4c073c3dc64507fb6c39bc20e46a48fhttps://github.com/zizmorcore/zizmor/releases/tag/v1.28.0https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f42p-wjw5-97qh

items.title: [code-graph-rag] Code Graph RAG: MCP paginated read_file path traversal / arbitrary file read
items.summary: SummaryThe read_file MCP tool in codebase_rag/mcp/tools.py contains a path traversal vulnerability in its paginated branch (when offset or limit is supplied). The handler constructs a file path using Path(self.project_root) / file_path without subsequently validating that the resolved path remains within the configured project root. Python's pathlib silently discards the left-hand component when the right-hand argument is an absolute path, allowing an attacker to read any UTF-8-readable file on the server by passing an absolute path such as /etc/passwd. DetailsVulnerable location: codebase_rag/mcp/tools.py:556–565 (MCPToolsRegistry.read_file)The read_file MCP tool accepts three parameters: file_path, offset, and limit. When either offset or limit is present the handler takes a distinct code path:# codebase_rag/mcp/tools.py:556-565async def read_file(    self, file_path: str, offset: int | None = None, limit: int | None = None) -> str:    logger.info(lg.MCP_READ_FILE.format(path=file_path, offset=offset, limit=limit))    try:        if offset is not None or limit is not None:            full_path = Path(self.project_root) / file_path   # ← VULNERABLE LINE            start = offset if offset is not None else 0            with open(full_path, encoding=cs.ENCODING_UTF8) as f:   # ← SINKBecause pathlib.Path.__truediv__ replaces the left operand entirely when the right operand is an absolute path, any caller-supplied absolute path (e.g., /etc/passwd, /proc/self/environ) causes full_path to point outside the project root.The non-paginated branch is protected by the @validate_project_path decorator (applied via codebase_rag/tools/file_reader.py:27) which performs .resolve().relative_to(project_root) (codebase_rag/decorators.py:73–75), but this decorator is never invoked in the paginated branch, leaving it completely unguarded.Full data-flow (source → sink):codebase_rag/config.py:302 — HTTP MCP default host is 0.0.0.0.codebase_rag/cli.py:717 — CLI exposes mcp-server.codebase_rag/cli.py:726–731 — --transport http invokes serve_http(host=resolved_host, port=resolved_port).codebase_rag/mcp/server.py:208–210 — Starlette mounts the MCP HTTP endpoint.codebase_rag/mcp/tools.py:227–249 — read_file is registered as an MCP tool accepting attacker-controlled file_path, offset, and limit.codebase_rag/mcp/server.py:113–127 — call_tool dispatches JSON arguments directly to the handler via await handler(**arguments).codebase_rag/mcp/tools.py:561–565 — paginated branch builds full_path and calls open(full_path) without any boundary check.The vulnerability is also present when using the stdio transport because the vulnerable code path does not depend on transport type; however, the attack is unauthenticated and network-accessible only when HTTP transport is configured.PoCPrerequisites:Docker installed.Repository cloned with the vuln-001/ artifacts present (Dockerfile, poc.py).Build and run:# From the repository root (parent of vuln-001/)docker build -t vuln001-poc -f vuln-001/Dockerfile .docker run --rm vuln001-pocThe Dockerfile installs the codebase_rag package from the local repository source, creates a "safe" project root at /tmp/safe-project-root, and runs poc.py.What the PoC does (poc.py):Pre-mocks the mgclient / pymgclient native C extensions (Memgraph client) so the package imports without a live database.Instantiates MCPToolsRegistry via object.__new__(), setting only self.project_root = "/tmp/safe-project-root" — matching what the real server does.Demonstrates the pathlib bypass: Path("/tmp/safe-project-root") / "/etc/hosts" resolves to Path("/etc/hosts").Calls registry.read_file("/etc/hosts", offset=0, limit=5) — the actual vulnerable method from the installed package.Asserts that real /etc/hosts content is returned, confirming full boundary bypass.Expected output:[MCP] read_file: /etc/hosts (offset=0, limit=5)[+] CONFIRMED: pathlib discards project_root when file_path is absolute[+] read_file() returned:# Lines 1-5 of 7127.0.0.1localhost::1localhost ip6-localhost ip6-loopbackfe00::ip6-localnetff00::ip6-mcastprefixff02::1ip6-allnodes[+] EXPLOIT SUCCESSFUL[+] Content of '/etc/hosts' exfiltrated via path traversal[+] Project root boundary '/tmp/safe-project-root' was completely bypassed[+] VULNERABILITY CONFIRMED: VULN-001 CWE-22 Path TraversalEquivalent HTTP transport attack (when server is running):python3 - <<'PY'import anyiofrom mcp import ClientSessionfrom mcp.client.streamable_http import streamablehttp_clientasync def main():    async with streamablehttp_client("http://127.0.0.1:8080/mcp") as (read, write, _):        async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:            await session.initialize()            result = await session.call_tool(                "read_file",                {"file_path": "/etc/passwd", "offset": 0, "limit": 10},            )            print(result.content[0].text)anyio.run(main)PYRemediation:--- a/codebase_rag/mcp/tools.py+++ b/codebase_rag/mcp/tools.py@@     async def read_file(

items.title: [fastapi-code-generator] fastapi-code-generator: Import-time RCE via route path -> unescaped @app.get('...') decorator
items.summary: Summaryfastapi-code-generator (koxudaxi) emits the OpenAPI path into the generated main.py route decorator as a single-quoted string literal (@app.get('/u/<path>/x')) without escaping the '. A ' in the path closes the decorator string and, via concatenation, injects a live expression that the decorator argument evaluates when main.py is imported (the ASGI server imports it at startup) -- code execution, no request needed. The path is a pure data field. Verified on fastapi-code-generator 0.8.0 / Python 3 / FastAPI.Details@app.get('/u/'+(__import__("os").system('…') or "")+'/x', response_model=None)def get_thing() -> None: passThe generator post-processes output with black/isort, so a syntax-breaking payload aborts generation (DoS); a valid-Python concat ('+expr+', kept valid with (… or "")) is written and runs at import. info.description (description='…'), tags, and parameter defaults are '-escaped; the path in @app.get('…') is the unescaped sink. Models come from datamodel-code-generator (repr-escaped, no RCE).Not a duplicate: distinct product from OpenAPI Generator's python-fastapi backend (different codebase/template/decorator); and distinct from the operation-summary docstring sink in the same product.PoCreproduce.sh (+ make_spec.py) attached: generates the app and merely imports main.py; the injected expression runs at decorator evaluation and writes a marker. Verified on 0.8.0.ImpactCode execution at import/startup in any application/CI that generates a FastAPI app with fastapi-code-generator from an attacker-controlled or attacker-influenced spec and imports/serves it. items.title: [fastapi-code-generator] fastapi-code-generator: Import-time RCE via response status-code key -> unescaped @app.get(..., responses={...}) dict
items.summary: Summaryfastapi-code-generator (koxudaxi) emits an operation's extra responses into the route decorator's responses={...} dict, using each response's status-code key as a single-quoted string literal without escaping the '. A ' in a status-code key closes the dict-key string and, via concatenation, injects a live expression that the decorator argument evaluates when main.py is imported (the ASGI server imports it at startup) -- code execution, no request. The status-code key is a pure data field. Verified onfastapi-code-generator 0.8.0 / Python 3 / FastAPI.Details@app.get( '/u', response_model=None, responses={ '404' + (__import__("os").system('…') or "") + 'x': {'model': Thing} },)def get_thing() -> None: passThe responses={...} dict is emitted only when the operation has a second (non-primary) response, so the malicious key is any additional response status. The generator post-processes with black/isort, so a syntax-breaking payload aborts generation (DoS); a valid-Python concat ('+expr+', kept valid with (... or "")) is written and runs at import. The response content-type key is NOT a sink (normalized to 'model'). info.* are repr-escaped; operationId -> function_name fails closed (DoS-resistant).Not a duplicate: same product as the path -> @app.get('…') and summary -> handler-docstring findings, but a different field (response status-code key) and position (the responses={...} decorator dict key). Distinct from OpenAPI Generator's python-fastapi. Models come from datamodel-code-generator (repr-escaped).PoCreproduce.sh (+ make_spec.py) attached: generates the app and merely imports main.py; the injected expression runs at decorator evaluation and writes a marker. Verified on 0.8.0.ImpactCode execution at import/startup in any application/CI that generates a FastAPI app withfastapi-code-generator from an attacker-controlled or attacker-influenced spec (multi-response operation)and imports/serves it. Estimated Critical, e.g. CVSS:4.0/AV:N/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:H/VA:H/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N.Suggested fixEscape each response status-code key for the Python string literal (escape ', , newlines via repr) before emitting the responses={...} dict, and validate that status-code keys are numeric / a known pattern. maintainer-report.txt make_spec.py reproduce.shReferenceshttps://github.com/koxudaxi/fastapi-code-generator/security/advisories/GHSA-6xmv-cjr5-w3q8https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63469https://github.com/koxudaxi/fastapi-code-generator/commit/49301dbdb82170d7f50877419d994b05cb1fa2bchttps://github.com/koxudaxi/fastapi-code-generator/commit/b3b9bd66e0b0c4d8c686fda700258104615a1332https://github.com/koxudaxi/fastapi-code-generator/releases/tag/0.8.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-6xmv-cjr5-w3q8

items.title: [fastapi-code-generator] fastapi-code-generator: Call-time RCE via operation summary -> unescaped route-handler docstring
items.summary: Summaryfastapi-code-generator (koxudaxi) emits an operation's summary as the generated route handler's docstring, using a triple-quoted string without escaping """. A """ in the summary closes the docstring and, via concatenation, injects a live expression that becomes an expression statement in the handler body -- which runs when the route handler is CALLED (the endpoint is hit). The summary is a pure data field. Verified on fastapi-code-generator 0.8.0 / Python 3 / FastAPI.Detailsdef get_thing() -> None: ( """ x""" + (__import__("os").system('…') or "") + """y """ ) passThe generator post-processes with black/isort, so a syntax-breaking payload aborts generation; a valid-Python breakout ("""+expr+""", kept valid with (… or "")) is written and executes at call time. info.description, tags, parameter defaults are escaped; operation description is not emitted into the function body; the summary in the handler docstring is the unescaped sink. Models come from datamodel-code-generator (repr-escaped, no RCE).Not a duplicate: distinct product from OpenAPI Generator's python-fastapi; and distinct field/sink from the route path -> @app.get('…') decorator (import-time) in the same product -- this is the operation summary in the handler docstring (call-time).PoCreproduce.sh (+ make_spec.py) attached: generates the app and calls the route handler; the injected expression runs and writes a marker. Verified on 0.8.0.ImpactCode execution on the server when the affected endpoint is invoked, in any app generated with fastapi-code-generator from an attacker-controlled or attacker-influenced spec.Suggested fixEscape the summary for the docstring context (escape """/backslashes via repr, or strip triple-quotes) before emitting it as the handler docstring; apply the same to any free-text field rendered into a docstring. maintainer-report.txt make_spec.pyreproduce.shReferenceshttps://github.com/koxudaxi/fastapi-code-generator/security/advisories/GHSA-h667-4jj2-cgv4https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-63470https://github.com/koxudaxi/fastapi-code-generator/commit/49301dbdb82170d7f50877419d994b05cb1fa2bchttps://github.com/koxudaxi/fastapi-code-generator/commit/b3b9bd66e0b0c4d8c686fda700258104615a1332https://github.com/koxudaxi/fastapi-code-generator/releases/tag/0.8.1https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-h667-4jj2-cgv4
